sticky.$description: Tier: Base — in-content sticky elements; stays below the page header.

header.$description: Tier: Base — the page's global header.

dropdown.$description: Tier: Floating on page — dropdown/select/popover/tooltip mounted directly on the base page (no drawer or modal open).

drawer-floating.$description: Tier: Drawer — use for dropdown/select/popover/tooltip mounted *inside* an open Drawer, instead of z.dropdown/popover/tooltip, so it renders above the drawer panel it lives in.

modal-floating.$description: Tier: Modal level 1 — use for dropdown/select/popover/tooltip mounted *inside* an open level-1 Modal.

modal-overlay-2.$description: Tier: Modal level 2 (a modal opened from within another modal)

modal-floating-2.$description: Tier: Modal level 2 — use for dropdown/select/popover/tooltip mounted *inside* an open level-2 modal.

toast.$description: Tier: Global notifications — always on top, independent of whatever drawer/modal is open.

z.$description: Named tiers with 100-point gaps (room to insert without renumbering) and, within Drawer/Modal tiers, a fixed 3-slot sub-pattern (overlay/panel/floating, +0/+10/+20). Floating UI (dropdown/popover/tooltip) is intentionally NOT one global z-index: a component must pick the '-floating' (or base 'dropdown/popover/tooltip') token matching the topmost context it is currently mounted inside — on the page vs. inside a Drawer vs. inside Modal level 1 vs. level 2 — so it always renders above its own container without ever floating above a container it isn't part of. That context-detection is a component-layer concern (e.g. a React context each Drawer/Modal provides to descendants), not solved by the tokens alone — build it when the Select/Popover/Tooltip components get built.
